questions.q: What are the two options for 'How to set record field values' on a Create Records element?
options: Manually, or from an existing record variable that already holds the values
Automatically, or never
Only by formula
Only by querying another object first
questions.explain: Create Records lets you set fields manually, one at a time, or use a record variable that already holds the desired values.

questions.q: On a before-save record-triggered flow, why can an Update Records element only 'Use the record that triggered the flow,' and not the other three lookup methods?
options: Before-save flows don't support Update Records elements at all
Before save, there's no saved record yet to look up elsewhere — only the one already in memory
The other three methods were removed from Flow Builder entirely
Update Records elements always require a Loop
questions.explain: A before-save flow runs mid-transaction, before the record is saved, so it can only act on the in-memory triggering record.

questions.q: What would you need to change to unlock Update Records' other three 'How to Find Records' methods, like updating related records?
options: Nothing — they're always available
Configure the flow's trigger to run the flow after the record is saved
Add a Loop element around the Update Records element
Switch the flow from record-triggered to scheduled
questions.explain: Running the flow after the record is saved allows Update Records to look up and update related or filter-matched records, not just the triggering one.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what level of caution does the Delete Records element deserve compared to Create and Update Records?
options: The same level of caution as the other two — no difference
Less caution, since deletions are automatically reversible
More caution — test thoroughly in a sandbox, and use it only for records that genuinely should never have existed
No caution is needed if conditions are specified
questions.explain: Delete Records removes data permanently, so it deserves more caution and sandbox testing than Create or Update Records.

questions.q: What's the shared underlying pattern across Create Records, Update Records, and Delete Records?
options: All three require a Decision element first
Find or build the target record(s), then act on them — set values, change values, or remove them
All three automatically loop over collections
All three only work on custom objects
questions.explain: Each element follows the same shape: locate or build a record, then either set its values, update them, or remove the record entirely.
